title: Default signing key and century-long refresh tokens create persistent credential risk
reasoning: If SECRET_KEY is not configured, the app falls back to a public hardcoded key. The default JWT refresh token lifetime is effectively permanent, so a deployment that misses SECRET_KEY or leaks refresh tokens has very long-lived tokens signed with a known secret. The test settings intentionally shorten JWT lifetime and override SECRET_KEY, so tests do not reflect the production default risk.
recommendation: Require SECRET_KEY in production instead of providing an insecure fallback, and reduce the default refresh token lifetime to a bounded operational value. If extremely long sessions are required, use rotation, revocation, and explicit environment-gated configuration.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: tests/test_settings.py replaces both SECRET_KEY and SIMPLE_JWT, masking the production defaults under review.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a configuration test asserting production settings fail fast when SECRET_KEY is unset and that refresh token lifetime stays below the chosen maximum unless an explicit production setting opts in.
minimumFixScope: Update SECRET_KEY loading and SIMPLE_JWT defaults in bahk/settings.py.
